question: JPMorgan Chase Software Engineer Intern (on-campus), Technical Round 1. After a resume deep dive, the candidate was given an array problem and started by sorting. The interviewer asked how they would sort without the library sort (STL `sort`). The candidate discussed merge sort (O(n log n)); the interviewer called it a big piece of code, so the candidate chose **quicksort**, explained the algorithm and began writing the code.
lookingFor: Knowing at least two O(n log n) sorts and comparing them honestly.
Writing a correct partition routine under time pressure.
Understanding worst cases (sorted input, duplicates) and how to mitigate them.
Clear complexity analysis and in-place versus extra-space reasoning.
followUps: What input makes quicksort quadratic with a last-element pivot, and how does a random pivot help?
How would you modify it to handle many duplicate values efficiently?
When would you pick merge sort instead (stability, linked lists, external data)?
How does quickselect find the k-th smallest element using the same partition?
